narrative.overview: nrum seq is a monitoring surface for an algorithm that is already running. The rosette, the cobweb, the phase circle and the attractor path are the product; the chrome around them is the instrument housing that lets you read and steer those drawings without competing with them. The surface is dark not to look technical but because a dark chamber is what makes a plotted signal legible: every bright mark on screen is data, and every dull mark is structure that must stay quiet enough to ignore. Density is the house style. The editor is a fixed 860x768 logical window holding a drawing, a mode description, sixteen parameter rows, an eight-lane matrix and a status strip. Nothing reflows; everything is placed. That constraint is why the type scale runs 9-14px and why weight and tone carry hierarchy rather than size. Precision is the ambition here, not expression.
keyCharacteristics: Dark chamber with one plotted signal and three accent hues doing distinct jobs.
Fixed 860x768 coordinate space; no responsive breakpoints, only deliberate placement.
Type named by job, not size, and dominated by 10-11px functional text.
Flat surfaces; depth from tonal layering, with shadows reserved for overlays.
Controls machined to the same spec as the drawings: slots, caps, ticks, 3-4px radii.

rules.name: The One Reading Rule
rules.body: At rest, a screen carries one drawing in the accent hues and one primary action in focus cyan. Everything else is neutral. Two saturated focal points means the hierarchy is wrong.

rules.name: The Signal Not Decor Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour is data. If a saturated element does not encode a value, a lane, or a state the user can act on, it is a bug.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Rule
rules.body: A label and its value share a row and differ in tone, not in size. If a value needs a larger type size to be found, the row is too wide.

rules.name: The 9px Floor Rule
rules.body: 9px exists for labels inside geometry that cannot grow (axis ticks, step badges). A control label at 9px is a layout failure, not a type choice.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: No surface inside the panel carries a shadow. If a control appears to float, it has been over-styled.

rules.name: The Solid State Rule
rules.body: A state fill is the accent at full opacity. A tint behind a label drops it below 4.5:1 in at least one theme; the tint is the defect, not the hue.

rules.name: The One Bloom Rule
rules.body: Motion has exactly one moment. Generate answers with a single accent bloom across the panel: 70ms to arrive, 450ms to leave. Nothing else in the chrome eases; state changes land on contact.

dos: Do keep saturated colour for data and state only; the neutral stack carries the structure.
Do place controls at their final position in the fixed 860x768 space rather than adding breakpoints or scroll regions to the main panel.
Do use 3-4px radii and 1px low-contrast borders; the surface should read as a panel, not a set of cards.
Do reserve 12px shadows for popovers and 16px for drawers, with the single shadow colour.
Do let one drawing and one action own the accent hues at rest.
donts: Don't use gradients as fills, glows, or glass. The one gradient is the accent ramp that marks a selected row, parameter or mode; it never appears as decoration.
Don't build a dark web dashboard: no purple, no translucent cards, no pill-shaped everything, no emoji as iconography.
Don't imitate a generic DAW: no brushed metal, no knobs, no tabbed preferences, no stock widget styling.
Don't build a sci-fi HUD: no scanlines, no neon wireframes, no hexagonal grids, no telemetry animation for its own sake.
Don't raise functional labels above 11px to create hierarchy; use weight and tone instead, and if that fails the layout is wrong.
